fact: The Northern Illinois Transit Authority (NITA), formerly the Regional Transportation Authority (RTA), is the regional transit agency for Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry, and Will counties; it sets regional fares, service standards, and schedules for CTA, Metra, and Pace.
NITA replaced the RTA on 2026-09-01.
conflict_or_note: No NITA web page states the date in its text (AEO-NITA-005); the fare portal and the board summary do.

fact: The NITA Act (Public Act 104-0457) took effect on 2026-06-01; it was signed in December 2025.
conflict_or_note: Signature month from Moving the system; the effective date from NITA's board summary (AEO-NITA-005).

fact: From 2026-08-01 the NITA sales tax is 1.25% (general merchandise) and 1.50% (qualifying food, drugs, and medical appliances) in Cook County, and 1.00% in DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry, and Will counties.
conflict_or_note: Conflict: Moving the system gives .50% in the collar counties plus a “New 2026 0.25%” (AEO-NITA-005). Official source: Illinois Department of Revenue bulletin FY 2026-34.

fact: CTA fares with Ventra: $2.50 on the ‘L’ and $2.25 on buses ($2.50 cash on buses); reduced fares $1.25 and $1.10.
conflict_or_note: Matches CTA (2026-11-24).

fact: Pace bus fare: $2.00 with Ventra and $2.25 cash; Premium routes $4.50.
conflict_or_note: Matches Pace (2026-11-24).

fact: Metra one-way fares by zone: $3.75 (zones 1–2 and 2–4), $5.50 (1–3), and $6.75 (1–4); reduced $1.75, $2.75, and $3.25.
conflict_or_note: Matches Metra (2026-11-24).

fact: The Regional Day Pass is sold only in the Ventra app: weekdays $10 (zones 1-1, 1-2, 2-3-4), $13.50 (1-3), and $16 (1-4), reduced $6, $8, and $9; $9.50 on weekends and holidays.
conflict_or_note: Matches metra.com/rdp (2026-11-25).

fact: On CTA, children under 7 ride free with a fare-paying customer; children 7 to 11 pay a reduced fare.
Reduced Fare Permits are for people aged 65 and over who are not eligible for Ride Free, people with qualifying disabilities, and Medicare card holders.
Apply online in the NITA Fare Programs portal (fares.nita.illinois.gov), at a registration site, or with a paper application; call 312-913-3110 for help or to have an application mailed.
conflict_or_note: The paper forms still show the RTA name and an RTA PO Box (AEO-NITA-002).

fact: Reduced Fare Permits do not renew automatically; renew in the NITA Fare Programs portal.
Older adults and people with disabilities enrolled in the Illinois Department on Aging’s Benefit Access Program can ride CTA, Metra, and Pace fixed routes free with a Ride Free Permit.

Households in the six counties that receive SNAP or IDHS FRESH benefits can get an Access Permit for reduced fares on CTA, Metra, and Pace (CTA and Pace since 2026-10-01); apply at GetAccess.org, and the permit arrives in 7 to 10 business days.
conflict_or_note: GetAccess.org redirects to the NITA Fare Programs portal.

fact: To apply for ADA Paratransit, call NITA’s ADA Paratransit Certification program at 312-663-HELP (4357).
conflict_or_note: Conflict on call hours: 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Accessible transit, 8:30 a.m. on Riders (SEO-NITA-027).

fact: ADA Paratransit is for people who, because of a disability, cannot use CTA or Pace fixed-route service for some or all trips; eligibility can be unconditional, conditional, or temporary. Pace operates the service; the fare is $3.25.
ADA Paratransit trips can be for any purpose; operators may not restrict or prioritize trips by purpose.
conflict_or_note: Not stated on NITA's website (AEO-NITA-004); official source is 49 CFR 37.131(d).

fact: NITA Travel Information: 312-836-7000.
conflict_or_note: Hours are not on NITA's website (AEO-NITA-004).

fact: NITA Ride Safe lets riders report safety concerns on CTA, Metra, and Pace by app or by texting 312.313.9015; it replaced Metra COPS and does not replace 911.

The proposed 2027 regional budget has $5.04 billion for operations (NITA, CTA, Metra, and Pace) and a $9.73 billion capital program for 2027–2031; public comments are accepted until 2026-12-04, and the board votes on 2026-12-10.
conflict_or_note: The budget page still invites readers to a past hearing (SEO-NITA-027).

fact: The next board meeting is on 2026-12-10 at 9:00 a.m. in the Board Room, 16th Floor, 175 W. Jackson Blvd., Chicago; public comments by email to communications@nita.illinois.gov by noon the day before.
conflict_or_note: Conflicts: “third Thursday of each month” versus second-Thursday meetings, a 1 p.m. start on the budget page, an RTA email behind the link (AEO-NITA-003); AI Overviews give Oak Park as the place (AEO-NITA-009).

fact: NITA is governed by a 20-member Board of Directors.
NITA Administrative Offices: 175 W. Jackson Blvd., Suite 1550, Chicago, IL 60604; 312-913-3200; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Customer service: 312-913-3110.
FOIA requests go in writing to NITA’s Freedom of Information Officer at 175 W. Jackson Boulevard, Suite 1550, or FOIA@nita.illinois.gov.
conflict_or_note: Conflicts: the page misnames the agency, its email link opens FOIA@rtachicago.org, and the linked form is addressed to the RTA at Suite 1650 (AEO-NITA-007).

fact: The People Over Parking Act took effect on 2026-06-01 and bars minimum parking requirements for new developments near transit; NITA offers municipalities technical assistance through an interest form.
My Transit Benefit is NITA’s pre-tax transit and parking benefit for employers and employees (the NITA Transit Benefit Fare Program), formerly run by the RTA, under Section 132(f) of federal tax law.
conflict_or_note: The website uses several names for the program and does not say in one passage who runs it (AEO-MTB-002).

fact: For 2026, employees can set aside up to $340 a month for transit and a separate $340 a month for parking.
conflict_or_note: Conflict: the homepage and Employers read as one combined $340 limit (AEO-MTB-001). The State of Illinois Commuter Savings Program page also gives $340 for 2026 (SEO-MTB-008 evidence).

fact: Employees can save up to 40% through reduced taxes; employers save on payroll taxes (7.65% on the homepage).
conflict_or_note: Conflict: the Employers calculator uses an 8.45% rate; no page explains the figures (AEO-MTB-001).

fact: The program offers the RTA/NITA Transit Benefit Prepaid Mastercard, Ventra Direct Loads (CTA, Pace, and Metra), and Pace Vanpool.
conflict_or_note: Only in the employer guide; the product sections on Behind the Benefits are empty (AEO-MTB-003).

fact: Funds are available on the 20th of each month; the card has a $2,000 maximum balance and Ventra loads a $500 limit.
conflict_or_note: Only in the employer guide (AEO-MTB-003).

fact: Employers pay no monthly or order fee with ACH debit; paying by credit card costs 4% of the order.
conflict_or_note: Only in the employer guide (AEO-MTB-003).

fact: Under the Illinois Transportation Benefits Program Act, in effect since 2024-01-01, covered employers in the defined area near fixed-route transit must offer employees a pre-tax transit benefit.
conflict_or_note: Conflicts: the page calls it the “Transit Benefits Program Act”, writes the 2024 start as upcoming, and says “more than 50” employees where legal summaries say 50 or more (SEO-MTB-008). Threshold to be confirmed by NITA's legal team; the reviewer does not resolve it.
